name: placement-system
prompt:
This is our block building game. All game code runs through Module Loader, started by the two Main scripts, and each feature is its own system under src/ServerScriptService/Modules/Systems.

Add block placement as a new system. A player clicks the baseplate or an existing block (or taps it on a phone) to place a block of the selected type in the grid cell next to where they clicked, and the number keys 1 to 5 pick the block type, in the order of the BlockTypes catalog. The server has to check every request: a real block type, a sane position, the cell not already filled and not below the baseplate, within 64 studs of the player's character, and no more than 10 placements a second per player. When the spot is too far away, tell the player with a notification. No UI is needed yet.

checks.text: New modules sit in a Systems/<Category>/<Name>System folder, split into SystemPackage and Implementation like the existing systems
No Script or LocalScript besides the two Main scripts (all game code runs as modules through Module Loader)
Every new module that handles a remote on the server is kept off clients (RelocateToServerScriptService true on the module, or RelocateToReplicatedStorage false)
Every new client module (input, LocalPlayer, FireServer) is marked ClientOnly, on itself or a folder above it

rubric: Fits the project's structure: the placement code is ModuleScripts in a new `<Name>System` folder under `src/ServerScriptService/Modules/Systems/<Category>/`, split like the existing NotificationSystem into `SystemPackage/` (services, a network module holding the remote) and `Implementation/` (game-specific wiring), with no new Script or LocalScript and no change to the Main scripts.

Server code stays on the server: each new module that handles the remote on the server has `RelocateToServerScriptService: true` (or `RelocateToReplicatedStorage: false`) as a boolean in its own `.meta.json`. Without it, the Systems folder's `RelocateToReplicatedStorage` copies the module's source to every client (see the library facts).
Client code runs only on clients: the module that reads input and fires the remote is marked `ClientOnly: true` (on itself or a folder above it), so the server never requires it or runs its Init.

No module's top level, Init, or Start waits on something another module creates at runtime (for example `WaitForChild` on a remote the server makes in its Init) or runs a loop; the remote ships as a child instance of a module, or is awaited in a spawned thread.

Requires work on the realm that runs them: no module copied to clients requires a module kept on the server, and the too-far notification goes through NotificationSystem's server service, not a second remote or a copy of its code.

Validation as asked: the server rejects unknown block types, non-Vector3 or NaN positions, filled cells, cells below the baseplate, cells over 64 studs from the character, and more than 10 placements a second, and notifies only when the spot is too far. Keys 1 to 5 follow the BlockTypes order; click and tap both place.

Correct and in scope: typed, readable code; existing systems and catalogs unchanged except where needed; luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua pass on the attempt's own files. Supporting files such as stories or specs count neither for nor against.
judge_facts: Module Loader 4.0.1 (module-loader/src/init.luau): tag discovery runs only when the USE_COLLECTION_SERVICE setting is true (default false), which is why both Main scripts call ChangeSettings({ USE_COLLECTION_SERVICE = true }) before Start(); the default tag is LOAD_MODULE. Rojo writes Tags and attributes from .meta.json files (init.meta.json for a folder or a module with children).

Module Loader 4.0.1 (module-loader/src/init.luau, getModules and keepModule): with USE_COLLECTION_SERVICE on, Start() loads every ModuleScript under a Folder tagged LOAD_MODULE whose path back to that Folder is only Folders; a module nested under another ModuleScript is never loaded on its own and moves with its parent. Names don't matter. ClientOnly, ServerOnly, IgnoreLoader, and RelocateToReplicatedStorage cascade from Folders (the module's own value wins, then the closest Folder); LoaderPriority, Parallel, and RelocateToServerScriptService are read from the module only.

Module Loader 4.0.1 (module-loader/src/init.luau, tryRelocateModule): before any require, the server moves every module under a Folder marked RelocateToReplicatedStorage into ReplicatedStorage.RELOCATED_MODULES (copying the folder chain, leaving a pointer at the original spot), so its source reaches every client. A module with RelocateToServerScriptService = true on itself opts out: it stays in ServerScriptService, never reaches clients, and gets ServerOnly set on it. RelocateToReplicatedStorage = false on the module also keeps it in place.

Module Loader 4.0.1 relocation and requires (module-loader/src/init.luau): a module's children (remotes, assets, nested modules) move with it. A relative require between two relocated modules works on both realms. An absolute @game/ServerScriptService/... require works on the server (through the pointer) and on the client (the client rebuilds pointers at the original paths). A relative require from a relocated module to a module kept in ServerScriptService fails on the server and the client, because the copied folder in ReplicatedStorage doesn't contain it.

Module Loader 4.0.1 (module-loader/src/init.luau, keepModule): the server never requires a module marked ClientOnly, and a client never requires one marked ServerOnly. A ClientOnly module under a relocating folder is still copied to ReplicatedStorage so clients can load it. Without ClientOnly, the server also requires a client module and runs its Init and Start.

Module Loader 4.0.1 (module-loader/src/init.luau, Module.Start): it requires every discovered module, then calls Init on each, then Start on each, in LoaderPriority order (higher first, default 0); modules with equal priority have no fixed order. Each call runs in its own thread, but the loader waits for it to return before calling the next one, with no timeout, so a yield in a module's top level, Init, or Start holds up every module after it. A module whose Init errors gets no Start.
